citations.title: Assessment and service plan requirements
citations.requirement: Before admission, a comprehensive assessment of physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition must be completed by a physician, physician assistant or APRN. It must be repeated at least annually and on a significant change in condition, including a diagnosis of Alzheimer's or a related dementia. IDPH may set more frequent skin-integrity and nutrition assessments by rule. A written service plan is mutually agreed by provider, resident and representative and reviewed at least annually or when needs change. On request the resident or representative gets a copy of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan. Text as amended by P.A. 104-0589.

citations.title: Issuance of license
citations.requirement: A full-time director must be 21+ with a high school diploma or equivalent plus qualifying experience (35(a)(2)). Staff must be sufficient in number and skill for 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs and must take ongoing training (35(a)(3)). All employees subject to the Health Care Worker Background Check Act must meet it (35(a)(4)). Applicant must file the Alzheimer's/dementia special care disclosure document (35(a)(7)). As a condition of licensure the director must complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years. Licenses last one year, state the physical location, issue and expiration dates, and are not transferable.

citations.title: Service requirements
citations.requirement: Defines medication reminders, supervision of self-administered medication and medication administration. Medication administration is by a licensed health care professional employed by the establishment. A certified medication aide may administer under RN supervision and delegation per Nurse Practice Act 50-75, except Schedule II controlled substances and any subcutaneous, intramuscular, intradermal or IV medication. Supervision of self-administered medication is under a licensed health care professional, or under RN delegation for a certified medication aide. IDPH sets procedures by rule. Services may be provided directly or by others arranged with resident consent.

citations.title: Civil penalties
citations.requirement: IDPH may assess a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation, with each day a separate violation. A penalty of up to $3,000 (also per day) may be assessed for caring for a resident who exceeds the care needs defined in the Act. Repeated technical infractions within a calendar year may become a Type 3 violation. IDPH may hold hearings on appeals.

citations.title: Alzheimer and dementia programs
citations.requirement: No admission or retention if the establishment cannot provide or secure appropriate care or lacks appropriately skilled staff. Residency is barred if the resident's condition has so deteriorated that residency is detrimental to the resident or others, or if the resident is dangerous and the danger cannot be eliminated. IDPH rule must identify a validated dementia-specific assessment standard with inter-rater reliability. That assessment is approved by the physician, or a PA/APRN with geriatric dementia experience. It is done before acceptance, annually, and on a change in condition. Annual and change-of-condition assessments must be signed by a physician. Establishments offering a special dementia program must disclose to IDPH and residents, ensure a designated representative, adopt wandering and evacuation safety policies, coordinate communications with family, provide cognitive stimulation and activities, staff appropriately, provide director and direct care staff dementia training, and have emergency procedures and staffing patterns. Pre-admission assessment tools must be validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment (150(g)).

citations.title: Amends 210 ILCS 9/15, 35, 70, 135 and 150
citations.requirement: Amends Sections 15, 35, 70, 135 and 150 of the Assisted Living and Shared Housing Act. Section 99 makes it effective on becoming law. The ILGA page shows Effective Date 7/24/2026.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: Requires sufficient qualified staff for 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs (a). Requires at least one direct care staff person on duty at all times with adult CPR training (including a skills demonstration) and current certification (b). Direct care staff must be 16+ at hire (c). Job descriptions must set minimum education and experience (d). Employee files must hold the items in (e) and (f). Records are kept for employment plus at least 12 months (g). Staffing must cover the services listed in (h). Personnel schedules must meet (i). Awake staff are required for residents who cannot self-move to safety (j). Shared housing needs at least one staff member on site at all times (k). Assisted living needs at least one staff member awake, on duty and on site 24 hours (l). Nurse Aide Registry check before hire, with no hiring of anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation (m). Licensed-staff license verification (n). Cornell shows this section's history as last amended in 2004, so check it against the current JCAR text.

citations.title: Establishment Contracts
citations.requirement: The contract must be titled 'assisted living establishment contract' or 'shared housing establishment contract' and printed in at least 12-point type. It must contain the 20 elements in (a), including: license status; base rate and services; extra services and fee schedule; complaint process with notice of the Department on Aging Senior Helpline and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; the Medicaid statement; admission and termination criteria; a risk management statement; and the Section 95 rights list. It must also include a statement from IDPH on the annual on-site review process. Under (b) it must include fee/deposit/refund terms, 30 days' written notice of fee changes (not required where service needs change per the service plan), and an emergency/relative notification policy. A copy goes to the resident or representative, and the signed contract stays on premises. Contracts may auto-renew yearly, and changes must be written and signed by both parties.

citations.title: License requirement
citations.requirement: No person may establish, operate, maintain or offer an assisted living or shared housing establishment without a license (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Renewal of licenses
citations.requirement: Renewal application is filed 120-150 days before expiration. IDPH 'may' grant a 2-year renewal at the licensee's request only if, in the preceding 24 months, there was no Type 1 or Type 2 violation, no inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, and no admission or retention in violation of Section 75 (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Application for License
citations.requirement: Nonrefundable fee of $2,000 + $20 per unit for assisted living, $1,000 for shared housing. The application states standard vs. floating licensure, includes liability insurance documentation, and shows financial capacity (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Initial license issuance
citations.requirement: IDPH issues a regular license within 120 days of a complete application. Approval needs fees paid, substantial compliance, and Background Check Act compliance for covered employees (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Residency Requirements
citations.requirement: An establishment may not accept or retain a resident when it lacks staff appropriate in numbers and skill, or cannot provide or secure the required services (per fact-checked research). Read the full text for the complete list of conditions.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act
citations.requirement: Covers employees with or who may have resident contact. Fingerprints are collected electronically and sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Supportive Living Program
citations.requirement: HFS rules for Medicaid Supportive Living. Applies only if the facility is separately approved and certified by HFS. It does not apply to an IDPH-licensed establishment that is private pay only.

citations.title: Assisted Living and Shared Housing Establishment Code
citations.requirement: Subparts, as confirmed on the LII table of contents: A General Provisions (295.1-295.1110); B Policies (295.2000-295.2080); C Personnel (295.3000-295.3050); D Resident Care and Services (295.4000-295.4060); E Medications (295.5000); F Resident Rights (295.6000-295.6030); G Resident and Establishment Records (295.7000-295.7010); H Food Service (295.8000); I Physical Plant and Environmental Requirements (295.9000-295.9040). policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Director/Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: Illinois statute says 'director'; the rules say 'manager'. Use both terms and keep them consistent.

The establishment must be under a full-time director who is 21+ with a high school diploma or equivalent plus 2 years of qualifying management or progressive-responsibility experience (health care, housing with services, adult day care or similar services to the elderly). The statute also allows a hospitality-experience-plus-training route, or a college degree in health administration or an approved program completed within 6 months of hire (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(2)).
The director must complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years as a licensure condition (210 ILCS 9/35).

Research states a shared housing manager may oversee up to 3 establishments within 30 minutes' drive and be immediately reachable, and that manager changes are reported to IDPH within 10 working days. Neither was pinpointed. Verify in 295.3010 and Part 295 text before publishing.
Name a qualified backup so the full-time director requirement is never unmet.

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: No person may establish, operate, maintain or offer an assisted living or shared housing establishment without an IDPH license (210 ILCS 9/25).
The license is valid for one year, names the physical location, and is issued only for the premises and persons named. It cannot be transferred or assigned (210 ILCS 9/35).

Renewal application and fee are filed 120-150 days before expiration. A 2-year renewal is discretionary and only if there was no Type 1 or Type 2 violation, no inspection with 10+ Type 3 violations, and no Section 75 admission/retention violation in the prior 24 months (210 ILCS 9/45).

Civil penalties: up to $5,000 per violation, each day separate; up to $3,000 per day for caring for a resident who exceeds the Act's care needs (210 ILCS 9/135). Correction to the research: the $3,000 figure is the care-needs penalty in 135(b), not an unlicensed-operation penalty. Confirm the penalty for unlicensed operation separately.

Initial fees: $2,000 + $20/unit (assisted living), $1,000 (shared housing), nonrefundable (295.500, per research). IDPH issues the regular license within 120 days of a complete application (295.600, per research).
The licensing application includes standard vs. floating licensure.
Track P.A. 104-0589 (effective 7/24/2026) and the pending Part 295 rulemaking in the Illinois Register.
Posting requirements for the license: not verified. Confirm in the rule text.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Annual review, plus a review trigger for every statutory or rule change. Immediate triggers: P.A. 104-0589 (effective 7/24/2026), which changes the assessment, director training, medication, dementia and penalty provisions.
Keep a version log. Each policy lists its Part 295 and Act citation.
Part 295 as published by LII shows amendments through 7/29/2024. Re-check ILGA/JCAR for later rulemaking before each annual review.

policies.title: Quality Improvement Program and Risk Management
state_specifics: 295.2060 requires a Quality Improvement Program; confirm the required elements, meeting frequency and documentation in the rule text.
The establishment contract must state that the establishment maintains a risk management process (295.2030(a)(18)).
Feed incident, grievance, fall, medication-error and infection data into the QI review.

policies.title: Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: IDPH-licensed assisted living and shared housing are private pay. The contract must state that Medicaid (Article V or VI of the Illinois Public Aid Code) is not available for services in the establishment (295.2030(a)(16)).
Billing must match the contract's base rate, additional-service fee schedule and billing procedures (295.2030(a)(7)-(9), (14)).

Only if the operator separately obtains HFS Supportive Living certification, add an SLP addendum under 89 Ill. Adm. Code 146. This includes quarterly quality-metric reporting through the HFS portal (per research). Otherwise state that SLP does not apply.
No Medicare/Medicaid certification-based compliance program applies to the private-pay licensure program.

policies.title: Annual IDPH On-Site Review and Survey Readiness
state_specifics: Added policy. The contract must include an IDPH statement describing the annual on-site review process and which resident-file documents the reviewer examines (295.2030(a)(20), citing Section 90 of the Act).
Keep resident files, contracts, assessments, service plans, personnel files, training records and schedules survey-ready at all times.
Name one IDPH liaison and keep a log of survey correspondence, deficiency responses and deadlines.
Type 1/2/3 violation history affects 2-year renewal eligibility (210 ILCS 9/45). Run internal mock reviews.

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Post and give residents the rights listed in Section 95 of the Act and 295.6000. The contract must list the Section 95 rights and state that contracting does not forfeit them (295.2030(a)(19)).
Pull the full rights list from the rule and statute text before drafting. It was not retrieved here.
Include resident responsibilities as stated in the contract (295.2030(a)(13), (b)(1)).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: The contract must describe the establishment's complaint resolution process and give notice of the Department on Aging's Senior Helpline and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (295.2030(a)(11)).
Add the IDPH complaint line and the Senior Helpline number to the form. Verify current numbers on IDPH and Department on Aging sites; they were not retrieved here.
Set response timeframes in the policy and log each grievance and outcome for QI review.

policies.title: Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: Residents must be told in the contract that the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program is available for complaint resolution (295.2030(a)(11)).
Post Ombudsman contact information. Verify the regional office and number with the Illinois Department on Aging.
Ombudsman access to residents: confirm the specific access rule in 295.6000 and Section 95.

policies.title: Establishment Contract, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: Title the document 'assisted living establishment contract' or 'shared housing establishment contract', in at least 12-point type.

Include the 20 mandatory elements in 295.2030(a). Include the (b) elements: fees, charges and deposits (including charges for absence days), the refund policy, and the emergency/relative notification policy.
Give 30 days' written notice before any change in a fee or charge. No 30-day notice is needed where the increase results from a documented service-plan change (295.2030(b)(4)).
Include the Medicaid-not-available statement (295.2030(a)(16)).
Give a copy to the resident or representative, and keep the signed contract on the premises for the residency (c)-(d).
Contracts may auto-renew yearly. Amendments must be written and signed by both parties (e). Termination by mutual agreement may be immediate (f).

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: The Part 295 rule text on handling resident funds and personal property was not retrieved. Confirm the requirements in 295.6000/Section 95 before finalizing.
Document any deposit and fee handling per the contract (295.2030(b)(2)-(3)).
Financial exploitation prevention applies (295.6010).

policies.title: Advance Directives
state_specifics: Confirm in the rule text whether Part 295 mandates advance directive handling. It was not retrieved.
Ask about advance directives and POLST at pre-admission, record them in the file, and make them available to staff and emergency responders per the service plan.
Illinois statutes on health care powers of attorney and POLST were not verified here. Have counsel confirm before publishing.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: HIPAA applies only to the extent the establishment or its providers are covered entities. Have counsel determine this; many private-pay assisted living operators are not covered entities, but state confidentiality still applies.
Residents or representatives may obtain, on request, a copy of their latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan (210 ILCS 9/15).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d)
state_specifics: The Act's 55+ age rule (at least 80% of residents 55+) is a definitional rule. Apply it consistently in admission marketing and decisions.
Provide interpretation and translated key documents (contract, rights, grievance process) to residents with limited English proficiency.
State-level nondiscrimination language in Part 295/Section 95: not retrieved. Confirm.

policies.title: Resident's Representative
state_specifics: 295.6030 governs the resident's representative; read the text before drafting.
The contract lists the resident's designated representative (295.2030(a)(12)). The representative takes part in service plan agreement (210 ILCS 9/15).
Dementia programs must ensure a resident's representative is designated (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(2)).

policies.title: Essential Support Persons
state_specifics: Added policy. 295.2080 governs essential support persons; the rule text was not retrieved. Obtain the designation process, access conditions (including during outbreaks or restrictions), and any documentation from the text before drafting.
Include the form for designating an essential support person.

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Before admission, a comprehensive assessment of physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition must be completed by a physician, PA or APRN. An RN or LPN cannot complete it (210 ILCS 9/15, as amended by P.A. 104-0589, effective 7/24/2026).
Reconcile the Physician's Assessment Form (Appendix A, version 3) and 295.4000 with the Act's PA/APRN language. Ask IDPH which form version to use.

Use a validated dementia-specific assessment tool for residents with cognitive impairment. IDPH rule must identify the standard. For dementia programs it must be approved by the physician, or a PA/APRN with geriatric dementia experience (210 ILCS 9/150(c), (g)).

Do not admit if the establishment cannot provide or secure appropriate care, the resident needs a service it is not licensed for or does not provide, or it lacks appropriately skilled staff (150(b); 295.2000).
Check Section 75 criteria (referenced in 150(e)) before every admission.
Confirm the at-least-80% age 55+ requirement before admission.

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: Comprehensive assessment at least annually, and upon a significant change in condition, including a diagnosis of Alzheimer's or a related dementia (210 ILCS 9/15).
IDPH may by rule require more frequent skin integrity and nutritional status assessments. Check 295.4000 and the current rule text.

For dementia programs, annual and change-of-condition assessments must be signed by a physician (210 ILCS 9/150(c)). A change may be identified by a family member, staff, or the resident's physician/PA/APRN.

policies.title: Service Plan
state_specifics: A written service plan is based on the assessment, the resident's interests, preferences, dislikes, and known triggers for behavior that endangers the resident or others. It is mutually agreed by the provider, the resident and the representative (210 ILCS 9/15).
Review at least annually, or sooner as condition, preferences or needs change. The service plan is the basis for the service delivery contract.
Give a copy to the resident or representative on request.
The plan may provide for disconnection or removal of any appliance (210 ILCS 9/15).
Services established in each service plan must be staffed (295.3000(h)(2)).

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Establishment Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Do not retain a resident when care or appropriate staff cannot be provided or secured, or the needed service is not licensed or provided (210 ILCS 9/150(b); 295.2000).
Dementia programs: no one may remain if their condition has deteriorated so that residency is detrimental to them or others, or if they are dangerous and the danger cannot be eliminated (150(c)-(d)).
Caring for a resident who exceeds the care needs defined in the Act exposes the establishment to a penalty of up to $3,000 per day (210 ILCS 9/135(b)).
The Section 75 criteria must be pulled from the Act text. It was not retrieved here.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer, Relocation and Closure Notice
state_specifics: 295.2010 (Termination of Residency) and 295.2020 (Notice of Closure) govern. Take notice periods, grounds and appeal procedures from the rule text, which was not retrieved.
The contract must describe admission and residency termination criteria and procedures (295.2030(a)(17)) and how the contract is terminated (a)(10).
Mutual-agreement termination may be immediate (295.2030(f)).
Notify the relative or other designated individual of termination of residency per the contract's notification policy (295.2030(b)(5)).

policies.title: Negotiated Risk Agreement
state_specifics: Added policy. 295.2070 governs negotiated risk agreements; the rule text was not retrieved. Take the required content and approval steps from the text, and have counsel review.
Use the agreement only for risks that do not make the resident ineligible under Section 75 or 150.

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Three levels of medication service are defined in the Act: medication reminders, supervision of self-administered medication, and medication administration (210 ILCS 9/70). Decide which the establishment offers. These are optional services.
Storage, labeling, disposal and record requirements are in 295.5000. Take the specifics from the text, which was not retrieved.
If residents cannot open containers, staff may open them for supervised self-administration (210 ILCS 9/70).

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
state_specifics: Medication administration (insulin and B-12 injections, oral medications, topical treatments, eye and ear drops, nitroglycerin patches, intramuscular injections) is performed by a licensed health care professional employed by the establishment (210 ILCS 9/70).

A certified medication aide may administer only under RN supervision and delegation per Nurse Practice Act Section 50-75. Excluded: Schedule II controlled substances and any subcutaneous, intramuscular, intradermal or IV medication.
Supervision of self-administered medication is under a licensed health care professional or, for a certified medication aide, under RN supervision and delegation.
Keep the authorized-staff list, credentials and delegation records on file.

policies.title: Nursing Services and Delegation
state_specifics: Medication aide delegation requires RN supervision (210 ILCS 9/70, citing Nurse Practice Act 50-75).
Mandatory services are in 295.4020. Define which nursing tasks the establishment provides.
Verify state professional licenses for staff in licensed positions with the Illinois professional regulation agency before hire and file a copy (295.3000(n)).

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: A significant change in condition triggers reassessment by a physician, PA or APRN (210 ILCS 9/15). For dementia residents the reassessment must be signed by a physician (210 ILCS 9/150(c)).
Notify the relative or designated person on a significant change in condition (295.2030(b)(5)).
Incident reporting timeframes: take from 295.2050 (text not retrieved).

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: Alzheimer and dementia programs must also comply with all other provisions of the Act (210 ILCS 9/150(a)).

An establishment offering a special program or unit must: disclose per the Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Special Care Disclosure Act to IDPH and to potential and actual residents; ensure a designated representative; adopt policies for continued safety of all residents including those who may wander or need help evacuating; coordinate communications with family; provide cognitive stimulation and activities; staff appropriately per rule; train the director and direct care staff in dementia care; and have emergency procedures and staffing patterns (150(f)).
The disclosure document is a licensure condition (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7)).
Assessments use a validated dementia-specific tool. Annual and change-of-condition assessments are signed by a physician (150(c), (g)).
Staffing numbers and training content are 'as established by rule'. Take them from 295.4060, which was not retrieved.
Memory care is not a separate license category in the research reviewed.

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: No Part 295 section specific to falls was identified. Falls are handled through the service plan (295.4010) and incident reporting (295.2050).
Track falls for QI (295.2060).

policies.title: Skin Integrity
state_specifics: IDPH may by rule specify circumstances for more frequent skin integrity and nutritional status assessments (210 ILCS 9/15). Check the current rule text for the frequency before setting your own.

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: Residents may receive services from providers the establishment does not contract with. The contract must say so (295.2030(a)(15)).
The contract must describe the license status of all providers of health-related or supportive services arranged by the establishment (295.2030(a)(5)).
Services may be provided by third parties arranged with the resident's consent (210 ILCS 9/70).
Hospice care does not lift the Section 75/150 admission and retention limits. Re-check retention with each change in condition.

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Notify the relative or other designated individual per the contract (295.2030(b)(5)).
Whether a death must be reported to IDPH, and any timing, are not verified. Check 295.2050.
Return personal property and refund fees per the contract's refund policy (295.2030(b)(3)).

policies.title: Mandatory Services
state_specifics: Added policy. 295.4020 lists the mandatory services; take the list from the rule text, which was not retrieved.
An establishment must provide all mandatory services and may provide optional ones (210 ILCS 9/70).
Staffing must cover mandatory services, service-plan services, environmental services, food service if offered, and emergency evacuation (295.3000(h)).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: 295.6010 governs prevention and reporting. Take reporting recipients, timeframes, training and investigation steps from the text, which was not retrieved.
Hiring bars: do not hire anyone with a Nurse Aide Registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property (295.3000(m)). Also screen under the Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

The reporting channels likely include IDPH, the Department on Aging Adult Protective Services program, and law enforcement. Phone numbers and the governing statute (the Adult Protective Services Act) were not verified. Confirm before publishing.

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: 295.2050 governs. Take the list of reportable events, deadlines and report contents from the text, which was not retrieved.
Feed incident data into the Quality Improvement Program (295.2060).

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Dementia programs must have policies ensuring the safety of residents who may wander (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(3)(A)).
Document elopement risk in the assessment and service plan. Staffing must provide general supervision (295.3000(h)(3)).

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: No restraint-specific rule was retrieved. Confirm in 295.6000/Section 95 and Subpart D.
Dementia programs must use policies that protect resident safety (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(3)).

Residents may not be retained if dangerous to self or others and the establishment cannot eliminate the danger through appropriate treatment modalities (210 ILCS 9/150(d)). Prefer discharge planning over restrictive practices.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: 295.2040 (Disaster Preparedness) governs. Take plan elements, review and drill frequencies from the text, which was not retrieved.
Staffing must cover evacuation of residents during emergencies (295.3000(h)(6)).
Dementia programs must have emergency procedures and staffing patterns (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(8)).
Residents who cannot move independently to safety require sufficient awake staff 24 hours a day (295.3000(j)).

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: IDPH Design and Construction performs the Life Safety Code survey before licensure (per research). Physical plant standards are in 295.9000 and the supplemental sections.
Evacuation capability: sufficient awake staff must be present for residents who cannot independently move to an area of safety (295.3000(j)).
Fire drill frequency, extinguisher and alarm testing: not retrieved. Take from 295.9000 and the Life Safety Code adopted by IDPH, and confirm with the local fire authority.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: 295.4040 requires communicable disease policies. Take required contents from the text, which was not retrieved.
OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard applies to employee exposure.
Outbreak reporting to the local health department and IDPH: not verified. Confirm requirements.

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Visitor access is subject to resident rights and the essential support person rule (295.2080, 295.6000).
No pet or smoking rule was retrieved. Check Subpart I (295.9040) and local ordinances. Illinois' smoke-free statute was not verified here.

policies.title: Communicable Disease Reporting and Tuberculin Screening Procedures
state_specifics: Added policy. 295.4040 (Communicable Disease Policies) and 295.4050 (Tuberculin Skin Test Procedures) both apply; take the content from the rule text, which was not retrieved.
Employees must have documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis in their file (295.3000(e)(2)(A)).

policies.title: Physical Environment, Heat Safety and Maintenance
state_specifics: Added policy. 295.9040 (Environmental Requirements) with Table A (Heat Index Table/Apparent Temperature) indicates heat-related environmental rules. Take the temperature thresholds and required actions from the text, which was not retrieved.
Units, furnishings and supplemental physical plant standards: 295.9005, 295.9010 (assisted living), 295.9020 (shared housing), 295.9030.

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Subpart H (295.8000) governs food service. Take menu, sanitation, diet and meal-time requirements from the text, which was not retrieved.
Food service employees need an initial health evaluation (295.3030).
Where the establishment provides food service, staffing must cover it (295.3000(h)(4)).

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Dementia programs must provide cognitive stimulation and activities to maximize functioning (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(5)).
Check 295.4020 for any activity requirements in mandatory services.

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Staffing must cover environmental services (295.3000(h)(5)).
Physical plant and environmental standards are in Subpart I.

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: Transportation is an optional service. List it with its fee schedule in the contract (295.2030(a)(8)-(9)).
Shared housing staff may leave the site briefly for a resident's emergency room trip or errands, but must arrange for monitoring resident safety per the service plan (295.3000(k)).

policies.title: Staffing Levels, 24-Hour Coverage and Supervision
state_specifics: Assisted living: at least one staff member awake, on duty and on site 24 hours a day (295.3000(l)).

Shared housing: at least one staff member on site at all times, with brief absences allowed for ER trips or errands if resident safety monitoring is arranged (295.3000(k)). The awake-overnight rule does not apply to shared housing by default. Residents who cannot independently reach safety require sufficient awake staff 24 hours a day (295.3000(j)).
At least one direct care staff person with current adult CPR certification (including a demonstrated skills check) on duty at all times (295.3000(b)).
The personnel schedule shows date, scheduled hours, and each employee's name and position, reflects actual hours worked, and is kept at least 12 months after the last scheduled date (295.3000(i)).
Staffing must meet the 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs of residents and cover the items in 295.3000(h). No fixed staff-to-resident ratio was found in the retrieved text.
Dementia programs: staffing 'as established by rule' (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(6)); check 295.4060.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Check every applicant on the Nurse Aide Registry before hiring. Do not hire anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property (295.3000(m)).

All employees subject to the Health Care Worker Background Check Act must meet it. This is a license-issuance condition (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(4)). Fingerprints are collected electronically and sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (225 ILCS 46, per research).
File documentation of Background Check Act compliance and the Nurse Aide Registry check in each direct care employee's file (295.3000(f)(3)-(4)).
Procedures are in 295.3040 (rule text not retrieved).

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Job descriptions define minimum education and experience (295.3000(d)). Direct care staff must be 16+ at the start of employment (295.3000(c)).
Orientation and ongoing training are documented in each file (295.3000(e)(2)(B)-(C)). Orientation content and hours: take from 295.3020, which was not retrieved.
Staff must take part in ongoing training for the resident population (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(3)).
Dementia programs: the director and direct care staff must complete dementia and cognitive deficit training, with content set by rule (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(7)).
Verify professional licenses for positions requiring them (295.3000(n)).

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Each direct care employee's file contains documentation of an initial health evaluation (295.3000(f)(2)).
Each employee's file contains documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis (295.3000(e)(2)(A)). Procedures: 295.3030 and 295.4050 (text not retrieved).
Keep employee health records for employment plus at least 12 months (295.3000(g)).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Every employee file has: name, date of birth, home address, Social Security number and phone number; documentation of freedom from pulmonary TB, orientation and ongoing training; and start and end dates (295.3000(e)).
Direct care files add: current CPR certification where applicable, initial health evaluation, Background Check Act compliance, and the Nurse Aide Registry check (295.3000(f)).
Keep records throughout employment and at least 12 months after the last date of employment or service, longer if state or federal law requires (295.3000(g)).
Licensed staff: place a copy of the license verification in the file (295.3000(n)).

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No Part 295 provision on staff conduct was retrieved. Tie this policy to the abuse, neglect and financial exploitation prevention rules (295.6010) and to employee exclusion for Registry findings (295.3000(m)).
Employee Assistance Programs are addressed in 295.3050. Text not retrieved.

policies.title: Director/Manager Qualifications, Training and Coverage
state_specifics: Added policy. Statutory director qualifications are in 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(2); manager qualifications are in 295.3010 (text not retrieved).
The director must complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years as a condition of licensure (210 ILCS 9/35).
Dementia programs: the director or administrator must complete dementia and cognitive deficit training per rule (210 ILCS 9/150(f)(7)).
Keep training certificates, qualification evidence and the named backup in the director's file.

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Subpart G (295.7000-295.7010) governs resident and establishment records. Take the required contents and retention periods from the rule text, which was not retrieved.
The signed contract is maintained on the premises for the whole residency (295.2030(d)).

Resident file includes the comprehensive assessment, supplemental assessments, service plan and signed contract (210 ILCS 9/15; 295.2030). The IDPH on-site review examines specified file documents (295.2030(a)(20)).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Annual license renewal application with fee, filed 120-150 days before expiration (210 ILCS 9/45).
Incident and accident reports per 295.2050 (text not retrieved).
Dementia disclosure document to IDPH if offering a special program (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7); 150(f)(1)).
Manager changes to IDPH within 10 working days (per research; section not pinpointed, check 295.3010 and the Part).
Health Care Worker Background Check submissions to Illinois State Police within 10 working days (225 ILCS 46, per research).
If SLP-certified: quarterly quality-metric reporting through the HFS SLP portal (per research).
